environment.description: Same Kubernetes pod but with a custom AppArmor profile loaded via annotation container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/log-processor=localhost/k8s-log-processor-restricted. The profile (stored at /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-log-processor-restricted) uses a deny rule set that restricts file write operations to an emptyDir-backed tmpfs at /var/log/app/current.log only (owner condition, exact path match). All other write paths including wildcard patterns like /var/log/app/*.csv and /var/log/app/metrics_* are explicitly denied. The profile also includes a 'deny /var/log/app/* w,' rule with an exception carved out via 'allow owner /var/log/app/current.log w,'. Since the CRLF injection's impact depends on writing forged entries to files that Fluentd monitors (which reads /var/log/app/*.log excluding current.log per its exclude_path configuration), and the AppArmor profile prevents the process from creating or writing to any file other than current.log, the injected content never reaches the log aggregation pipeline.
